inspiration.observed_pattern: A MySQL application upserts keyed records with ON DUPLICATE KEY UPDATE and separately reads a deterministic, ordered, limited leaderboard page.
inspiration.mysql_mariadb_translation: Reduced to one existing score and two staged scores. A deterministic ORDER BY with LIMIT 2 selects the existing row and one new row for an INSERT ... SELECT upsert; the lower-ranked staged row is not applied.

fixture_notes: Entry 8101 is refreshed, entry 8102 is inserted, and entry 8103 remains absent because LIMIT 2 selects the first two ordered rows.
determinism_notes: Points descending plus entry ID ascending defines the selected source subset. All keys and values are fixed; no clocks, randomness, sleeps, or concurrent connections are used.
setup: CREATE TABLE score_board_min (entry_id INT PRIMARY KEY, player_name VARCHAR(32) NOT NULL, points INT NOT NULL, tier VARCHAR(16) NOT NULL)
CREATE TABLE score_refresh_min (batch_id INT NOT NULL, entry_id INT NOT NULL, player_name VARCHAR(32) NOT NULL, points INT NOT NULL, tier VARCHAR(16) NOT NULL, PRIMARY KEY (batch_id, entry_id))

steps.sql: INSERT INTO score_board_min (entry_id, player_name, points, tier) SELECT entry_id, player_name, points, tier FROM score_refresh_min WHERE batch_id = 3 ORDER BY points DESC, entry_id LIMIT 2 ON DUPLICATE KEY UPDATE player_name = VALUES(player_name), points = VALUES(points), tier = VALUES(tier)

checks.sql: SELECT entry_id, player_name, points, tier FROM score_board_min ORDER BY entry_id
SELECT batch_id, entry_id, player_name, points, tier FROM score_refresh_min ORDER BY batch_id, entry_id
